source: Public YouTube search on 31 Oct 2026. Instagram does not publish a format count, so this is the demand signal, not an Instagram view counter.

formats.title: AI baby comedy skit
formats.signal_title: Baby Gaya Nani Ke Ghar Bina Bataye
formats.lasts: One random baby dies in about a week. The same face, same voice, and same set can keep going.
formats.what: A generic baby, an adult voice, one place, and a 30-second joke. Setup, complaint, punchline. This search returned several videos over 800,000 views on 31 Oct 2026, ahead of the other formats below.
make: Save one baby face. Do not use a real child's photo.
Keep one set, such as a shop counter or a house door, in every episode.
Write four lines: a request, a pause, a complaint, a last line.
Record your own voice. Do not clone a real person's voice.
Turn the still into a talking clip, then put big captions on every line.
Turn on Instagram's AI label. Post the next four episodes with the same baby.
formats.tools: A still generator, your own voice, and a talking-photo tool. CapCut for captions.
formats.avoid: A real child's face, a copied voice, or another channel's exact story.

formats.title: Character dance swap
formats.signal_title: Baby AI Dance Video Kaise Banaye
formats.lasts: A dance sound peaks in a few days. A character people recognize can outlast the sound.
formats.what: A still photo is placed onto a dance clip. The body moves, the face stays the character. On 31 Oct 2026 the top public result for this search was about 208,000 views, well below AI baby comedy.
make: Pick a dance clip you can use, 8 to 15 seconds, one person in frame.
Use a character you made. Do not use a living person's photo.
Upload the still and the dance into a motion tool and export 9:16.
Keep the same character next time. A new face every video does not become a channel.
Label the video as AI.
formats.tools: A motion tool such as Viggle or Kling, plus CapCut.
formats.avoid: A private person's face, or a celebrity's face, on the dance.

formats.title: AI talking-character series
formats.lasts: A one-off pretty face fades. A character with the same look and a point of view can run for months.
formats.what: One young-woman character, same face every episode, short clever lines to camera. This is the format behind those channels. On 31 Oct 2026 the top public result in this search was about 155,000 views.
make: Design one original face and save it. Do not copy a real creator.
Write a 20-second line with one turn at the end.
Record your own voice or a voice you have the rights to.
Lip-sync the still. Same clothes, same room, so the channel is recognizable.
Label it as AI.
formats.avoid: Copying a real creator's face, name, or exact videos.

formats.title: AI mythology clip
formats.signal_title: Ganesha vs Kartikeya — Race Around the World
formats.lasts: A single myth clip can spike. A series with the same art style lasts longer than a new god every upload.
formats.what: A short retelling of a known story, told in vertical video with AI images. On 31 Oct 2026 a public story result sat around 102,000 views. Tutorials about making these videos are common, which means many people are entering.
make: Pick one story you can tell in 30 seconds. One event, not the whole epic.
Open on the conflict in the first two seconds.
Use one art style for the whole series.
Captions on every line. A calm voiceover, not a song on top of the words.
Label it as AI.
formats.tools: Still or video generator, your voice, CapCut.
formats.avoid: Stuffing five scenes into 15 seconds. The viewer never reaches the ending.

formats.title: AI horror episode
formats.signal_title: Make Viral AI Horror Stories In Minutes (tutorial)
formats.lasts: Episode series last longer than one jump-scare. Number the episodes.
formats.what: A narrator, a dark still, and a story that ends on a turn. On 31 Oct 2026 this search mostly returned tutorials, the largest about 662,000 views. That is demand from people who want to make them, not a clean count of horror episodes. Treat this rank as softer than the baby skits.
make: Episode number on screen from the first second.
Write 80 words. A normal start, one wrong detail, a last line that reframes it.
One narrator voice for the whole series.
Three stills only. Cut on the sentences, not on a beat drop.
End on the turn. Do not explain it.
Label it as AI.
formats.avoid: Real people's faces, gore close-ups, and a new narrator every episode.
